title: One-Pot Cheeseburger Macaroni
subtitle: ground beef, macaroni and a creamy old cheddar sauce cooked together in one pot: homemade, better than the box
imageAlt: Creamy cheesy macaroni with ground beef in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Use a large deep skillet or Dutch oven with a lid; the pasta cooks right in the sauce.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Cook the beef and onion in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Spoon off the fat.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add the garlic, tomato paste, paprika, onion powder, salt and pepper and stir 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer the pasta
steps.text: Stir in the broth, milk, ketchup, Worcestershire and macaroni. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 10–12 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.

steps.title: Cheese
steps.text: Take off the heat and stir in the cheddar until melted and creamy. Rest 2 minutes; it thickens as it stands.

fixIt.fix: Keep the heat low and stir every 2–3 minutes; add a splash of broth if it gets thick before the pasta is tender.
The cheese went in over the heat. Stir it in off the heat, and shred your own if pre-shredded clumps.
Let it stand 3–4 minutes uncovered; the pasta keeps absorbing.

saleTip: Elbow macaroni is often 2 for $3 at No Frills; old cheddar blocks are cheaper than bags, so shred your own.
swap: Ground turkey: same amount, cooked to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Reheat with a splash of milk; it firms up in the fridge.
doneness: Ground beef cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada); pasta tender.
source: Based on tested one-pot cheeseburger pasta methods (Canadian Living, Food Network Canada): browned beef, macaroni simmered in broth and milk, finished with cheddar off the heat.
gear: Large deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid
prepAhead: Best fresh; it's ready in 35 minutes.
reheat: Covered in a pan over medium-low with a splash of milk, stirring, or in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beef, macaroni and cheddar with salt and pepper.

stepNotes.1: Basic: tomato paste, salt and pepper only.

fancy.note: Crispy bacon and diced pickles over the top, like the burger.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: first fry the chopped bacon in the pot until crisp, scoop it out and pour off all but 1 tbsp fat before browning the beef.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Scatter the bacon and pickles over each bowl.

plating: Bacon and pickles scattered on top.
Ketchup on the table, like burger night.

why.1-4: Cooking the pasta in the broth and milk thickens the sauce with its starch; no extra pot or roux.
why.1-5: Old cheddar has more flavour, so the sauce tastes cheesy without being heavy.

funFact: Boxed 'hamburger dinners' launched in 1971; making it from scratch takes the same time.

keeps.note: the pasta goes soft and the sauce splits
